hypothesis: After recent SPY/QQQ distribution pressure, a high-volume market follow-through day may identify liquid stock leaders with cleaner next-open 10-day replacement value than ordinary momentum.
interpretation: The market follow-through day leadership source did not clear Gate 4 or the accepted distribution-day comparator. Do not promote or retry this fixed OHLCV confirmation-day definition on the same frozen windows without materially new PIT flow or forward replacement-value data.
negative_reflection: If negative, the likely reason is that the classical follow-through-day label collapses into crowded high-beta rebound momentum after next-open execution and costs, while the accepted distribution absorption helper already captures the cleaner post-pressure setup.
next_evidence_needed: A retry needs materially new PIT flow evidence such as constituent fund-flow, options/borrow pressure, or closed forward replacement rows. Do not retune distribution counts, index-volume thresholds, hold days, cooldown, or paper notional on this frozen sample.

prediction.confidence_reason: Distribution-day absorption leadership was accepted, but broad momentum and pocket-pivot relabels often failed. This fixed source requires prior SPY/QQQ distribution pressure plus a high-volume index follow-through day and single-stock leadership, all from free PIT OHLCV. The main risk is that it just rediscovers high-beta momentum and fails the accepted distribution-day comparator.

production_impact.parity_note: This experiment changes no production code. A positive result would remain a replay lead until a shared default-off adapter computes the same prior distribution-pressure context, market follow-through-day confirmation, stock leadership fields, same-ticker core-overlap exclusion, next-open paper entry, 10-trading-day exit, costs, cooldown, comparator, and concentration controls in both historical replay and daily production.
